summary:
The EVA (Extra-Vehicular Activity) Route Planner is designed to help astronauts explore the surface of Mars safely and efficiently. Focusing on the Jezero Delta region, it identifies suitable routes from the habitat to scientific locations and back.

Users can select three scientific objectives: clay-bearing rocks, carbonate outcrops and olivine-rich formations. The system uses the A* pathfinding algorithm to calculate efficient routes while avoiding steep and potentially dangerous terrain.

Safety is prioritised through adjustable slope limits and different environmental conditions, including dust storms and solar particle events. It also includes map layers displaying slope hazards and thermal differences between sand and rock.

Once a route is generated, the system displays the distance, estimated walking time, steepest slope, maximum distance from the habitat and approximate radiation exposure.

The project uses synthetically generated terrain and mineral data to demonstrate its functionality. However, its routing algorithm and safety calculations could be adapted to use actual NASA data.

Overall, the project demonstrates how computational algorithms and terrain analysis can support safer and more efficient human exploration of Mars.
